***__Key Points__**

__
 
• *​*We use for to talk about a purpose or a reason for something.

• **Example**: *She arrived **with** her boyfriend.*
 
 
 
• *​*We use** in** to talk about where something is in relation to a larger area around it.
 
 
• **Example**: *She’s** in** the garden.*
 
 
 
• *​***Number of** is used with countable nouns.
 
 
• **Example**: *A great **number of **students volunteer each year for environmental projects.*

• A preposition is a word or group of words used before a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase to show direction, time, place, location, spatial relationships, or to introduce an object.
 
• Some examples of prepositions are words like *"in," "at," "on," "of," and "to."*
 
 
• Example: *I live in Raipur.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'to carry.'

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The construction **“to + verb”** is a formal construction that is used either a) to give an instruction or command, or b) to tell what is going to happen in the future.
 
• An infinitive verb is essentially the base form of a verb with the word **"to" **in front of it.
 
• When you use an infinitive verb, the **"to"** is a part of the verb and it is not acting as a preposition in this case.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 'to carry.'
 
• *​​*Correct phrase__: **........ **ess, often using donkeys **to carry** pots, pans and other wares to be sold.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 

__
 
• Infinitives are never conjugated with** -ed or -ing** at the end because they are not used as verbs in a sentence.
 
• They’re one of the three types of verbals, which are verbs used as an adjective, noun or adverb.
 
• The other verbals are gerunds and participles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• ​Construction “to + verb” एक औपचारिक निर्माण है जिसका उपयोग या तो ए) निर्देश या आदेश देने के लिए किया जाता है, या बी) यह बताने के लिए कि भविष्य में क्या होने वाला है।
 
• एक इनफिनिटिव क्रिया अनिवार्य रूप से एक क्रिया का मूल रूप है जिसके सामने **"to"** शब्द होता है।
 
• जब आप एक इनफिनिटिव क्रिया का उपयोग करते हैं, तो **'to'** क्रिया का एक हिस्सा है और यह इस मामले में एक पूर्वसर्ग के रूप में कार्य नहीं कर रहा है।

• There are modal verbs that do not change – ***Could, Would, Should, Might, Ought to***

• Let's learn the use of various conjunctions:

 
 
• Coordinating Conjunctions: They join like with like. In other words, they join a noun with another noun or an adjective with another adjective. There are seven in total: *for, and, nor, but, or, yet, *and *so*.

 
 
• Example: *He was late for school, so he took a shortcut.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

We’ll accept your application _______ you fulfil all the conditions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'provided.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Provided** means if something happens.

 
 
• Provided का मतलब होता है बशर्ते ।​

 
 
• **Example**: *You can go outside and play, **provided** you finish your homework on time.*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​***“So that”** is a conjunction that is used to join two clauses. ( one of them expresses an action, the other expresses the purpose )** “so that”** is used before the clause which indicates the purpose.
 
 
• *​*“So that” एक संयोजन है जिसका उपयोग दो खंडों को जोड़ने के लिए किया जाता है। (उनमें से एक क्रिया व्यक्त करता है, दूसरा उद्देश्य व्यक्त करता है) “so that” उस खंड से पहले प्रयोग किया जाता है जो उद्देश्य को इंगित करता है।
 
 
 
• We use** “so + that” **as a conjunction to introduce clauses of reason and explanation.
 
 
• हम कारण और स्पष्टीकरण के खंड को पेश करने के लिए संयोजन के रूप में “so + that” का उपयोग करते हैं।​
 
 
• **Example**: *We left a message with her secretary **so that **she would know we have come.*
 
 
 
 
 
• **Although** is all used to link two contrasting ideas or show that one fact makes the other fact surprising.
 
 
• Although सभी का उपयोग दो विपरीत विचारों को जोड़ने या यह दिखाने के लिए किया जाता है कि एक तथ्य दूसरे तथ्य को आश्चर्यजनक बनाता है। ​
 
 
• **Example**: *I enjoyed the course, **although** I would have liked more grammar practice.*
 
 
 
 
 
• We use **even if **when we’re talking about an unreal situation.
 
• जब हम किसी अवास्तविक स्थिति के बारे में बात कर रहे होते हैं तब भी हम even if का उपयोग करते हैं।
 
 
• We use it when we’re speculating or when we don’t consider something as a fact. 
 
• **Example**: *I’m going out tomorrow **even if** it’s raining.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct option is 'provided.'
 
• ​​The correct sentence__:* **We’ll accept your application **provided** you fulfil all the conditions.*

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• We use **even** when we want to express a surprising extreme or when we want to say that something is more than we expect.

 
 
• **Example**: *She’s rude to everyone. She’s **even** rude to me*.

**Direction: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

I am indebted to my friends for the large sum of money what they gave me during my days of need.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'what they gave me****.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in 'what they gave me' part of the sentence.
 
• **"That"** can introduce an explanatory dependent clause and **"What"** cannot.
 
• **"That" **indicates specific quality of the object in question or a subset of a larger set.
 
 
• Example: *This is the cat that killed the rat.*
 
 
 
• **"What"** indicates the object in the question itself, or the entire larger set.
 
 
• Example: *What would you like to do?*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the use of 'what they gave me' should be replaced by' that they gave me' to make it grammatically correct*.*
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'what they gave me.'
 
• *​​*Correct sentence__: *I am indebted to my friends for the large sum of money **that they gave me** during my days of need.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 

 

 *

__
 
• The present tense is the base form of the verb.
 
• We use do and does to make questions with the present simple.
 
• We use does for the *third person singular (she/he/it)* and do for the others.
 
• We use do and does with question words like *where, what *and* when.*
 
 
• Example: *Where do Angela and Rita live?*
 
 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** 

 

 *

 
• त्रुटि वाक्य के भाग 'what they gave me' में है।
 
• "That" एक व्याख्यात्मक आश्रित खंड पेश कर सकता है और "What" नहीं कर सकता।
 
• "That" प्रश्न में वस्तु की विशिष्ट गुणवत्ता या बड़े सेट के सबसेट को इंगित करता है।
 
 
• **Example**: *This is the cat **that** killed the rat.*
 
 
 
• "What" प्रश्न में ही वस्तु या पूरे बड़े सेट को इंगित करता है।
 
 
• **Example**:** *****What **would you like to do?*
 
 
 
• इसलिए वाक्य के 'what they gave me' प्रयोग को 'that they gave me' से बदल देना चाहिए ताकि वह व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही हो।​

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

During winters in Delhi, flights are oftenly cancelled due to heavy fog.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**oftenly cancelled**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given above sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• '**Often**' is not an adjective and '**oftenly**' is not an adverb.
 
• An **adverb **is a word that **modifies a sentence, verb, or adjective**.
 
• As per the general rule, "**Often**" is an adverb meaning ‘**many times on different occasions**’. 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *I have often wondered what happened to him. (correct)*
 
• *I have oftenly wondered what happened to him. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• *​*Here, in the given above sentence, '**oftenly**' is used as an adverb which is wrong.
 
• According to the explanation that is given above, ‘often’ is the correct use in place of “oftenly”.

**Correct sentence: ***During winters in Delhi, flights are **often** cancelled due to heavy fog.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

__
 
• ऊपर दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• '**Often**' एक विशेषण नहीं है और '**oftenly**' एक क्रिया विशेषण नहीं है।
 
• क्रिया विशेषण एक ऐसा शब्द है जो किसी वाक्य, क्रिया या विशेषण को संशोधित करता है।
 
• सामान्य नियम के अनुसार, "**often**" एक क्रिया विशेषण है जिसका अर्थ है **'कई बार विभिन्न अवसरों पर'**।
 
• **उदाहरण**:
 
 
• I have often wondered what happened to him. (**सही**)
 
• I have oftenly wondered what happened to him. (**गलत**)
 
 
 
• यहाँ, ऊपर दिए गए वाक्य में, '**oftenly**' का प्रयोग क्रिया विशेषण के रूप में किया जाता है जो गलत है।
 
• ऊपर दी गई व्याख्या के अनुसार, "**oftenly**" के स्थान पर '**often**' का सही प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

__
 
• * *It's easy to assume that all **adverbs end** in '**-ly**', since so many do, **but that isn't always the case**. Here is a **list of adverbs that don’t end in '-ly'**: (यह मान लेना आसान है कि सभी क्रियाविशेषण '-ly' में समाप्त होते हैं, क्योंकि कई करते हैं, लेकिन हमेशा ऐसा नहीं होता है। यहाँ क्रियाविशेषणों की एक सूची दी गई है जो '-ly' में समाप्त नहीं होते हैं:)

 
 
• "Already, often, quick, never, hard, late, etc."
 
 
 
• **Examples: **
 
 
• *We **already **knew that he was coming to visit. (correct)*
 
• *We **alreadyly **knew that he was coming to visit. (incorrect)*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The old telephone ______ nobody wants has been thrown into the junkyard.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**which**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pronouns that connect a clause or phrase to a noun or a pronoun, **is called **relative pronoun**.
 
• The **most common relative pronouns are**:
 
 
• “who, whom, whose, which, that”.
 
 
 
• As per the general rule, we use '**which**' in relative clauses **to refer to animals and things**, to introduce defining and non-defining relative clauses.
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• *You need to tick the box **which **says yes.​ ​(correct)*
 
• *You need to tick the box **who/whom **says yes.​ ​(incorrect)*
 
 
 
• *​*According to the explanation and example that are given above, **‘**which' is the correct choice for the given blank.

**Complete sentence:** *The old telephone which nobody wants has been thrown into the junkyard.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As per the general rule, we use 'who' in relative clauses **to refer to a person (as the verb’s subject)**.
 
• **Example:** 
 
 
• *The woman **who **came to the door left flowers for you. (correct)*
 
• *The woman **which **came to the door left flowers for you. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• As per the general rule, we use 'whom' in relative clauses to refer to a person (as the verb’s object).
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• *I am not sure **whom **this book belongs to. (correct)*
 
• *I am not sure **which **this book belongs to. (incorrect)*

questions.question:
**Given below are six sentences. A and F are the first and the last sentences. The rest of the sentences namely B, C, D and E are jumbled. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. It was noon and by now the two bandits were very hungry.

B. Now the one who was guarding the treasure thought, “It is a pity that this treasure has to be divided between two.”

C. So they decided that one of them would stay near the treasure and guard it.

D. And the other one would go to the neighbouring village and buy some food.

E. The one who stayed back placed his sword near the treasure and kept guard while the other set off in the direction of the village.

F. “It would be so much simpler if I could take it all.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**ACDEBF**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Sentence ‘C’** comes first as it is independent of any other sentence and introduces **when both of them decided to talk among themselves to quench the hunger**, So it will be put in the **first place**.
 
• **Sentence ‘D’** follows **‘C’** as it talks about **after the verdict, one stayed there near the treasury and the other went to a nearby village to buy some food**, and gives some information about the previous sentence, So it will be put in the **second place**.
 
• **Sentence ‘E’** follows **‘D’** as it states that, **one of the two stopped for protection by placing a sword near the treasure and the other left for the village**, as per mentioned in the given above sentence, So it will be put in the third place.
 
• **Sentence ‘B’** follows **‘E’** as it tells that, **the one who stood guarding the treasure thought, "It would be a pity to divide this treasure between two****"**, so **sentence B** is the concluding sentence. So it will be put in the fourth place.
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that **the correct order** is ‘**ACDEBF**’.
 
• **Thus, the sequence becomes:**
 
 
• **​**A: It was noon and by now the two bandits were very hungry. (दोपहर हो चुकी थी और अब तक दोनों डाकू बहुत भूखे थे।)
 
• C: So they decided that one of them would stay near the treasure and guard it. (इसलिए उन्होंने फैसला किया कि उनमें से एक खजाने के पास रहेगा और उसकी रखवाली करेगा।)
 
• D: And the other one would go to the neighbouring village and buy some food. (और दूसरा पास के गाँव में जाकर कुछ खाना खरीदता।)
 
• E: The one who stayed back placed his sword near the treasure and kept guard while the other set off in the direction of the village. (जो पीछे रह गया, उसने अपनी तलवार खजाने के पास रख दी और पहरा दे दिया, जबकि दूसरा गाँव की ओर चल पड़ा।)
 
• B: Now the one who was guarding the treasure thought, “It is a pity that this treasure has to be divided between two.” (अब जो खजाने की रखवाली कर रहा था, उसने सोचा, "यह अफ़सोस की बात है कि इस खजाने को दो के बीच विभाजित करना पड़ रहा है।")
 
• F: “It would be so much simpler if I could take it all.” ("अगर मैं यह सब ले सकता तो यह बहुत आसान होगा।")

• **Helping verb** **comes before the object** in the **passive voice,** (as passive voice start with object of the active voice)
 
• Convert the** verb into past participle or 3rd form** of the verb.
 
• Complete the sentence with the subject and **sign of Interrogation (?)**.
 
 
 
• Let's have a look at the **structural form** of the given rule:
 
 
• **Who/Why/When/How + auxiliary + subject + verb + object ? (active voice)**
 
• **By whom/Why/When/How + auxiliary + object + V3 + by + subject? (passive voice)****​**
 
 
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the** interrogative Sentences that start with the word 'Wh'.**
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• ***​**Who wrote this letter? (active voice)*
 
• *By whom was this letter written? (passive voice)**​*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘By whom are the accounts of this hotel kept?’ is the correct passive form of the given sentence.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Professor Sehgal will organise a webinar on investment tomorrow.

options.text: A webinar on investment is being organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.
A webinar on investment will have been organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.
A webinar on investment will be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.
A webinar on investment is going to be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**A webinar on investment will be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given above sentence is in an '**active voice form**', hence we need to convert it into a '**passive voice form**'.
 
• In an **active voice**, a **sentence emphasizes the subject**, performing an action.
 
• In a **passive voice**, a **sentence emphasizes the action or the object** of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice** and '**Professor Sehgal**' is the **subject **and '**a webinar**' is the **object**.
 
• When we** convert this sentence into passive voice**, the **subject **'Professor Sehgal' of the active voice **becomes the object**, the object 'a webinar' becomes the **subject**.
 
• Let's have a look at the **structural form** of the given rule:
 
 
• **​Subject + will/shall + V1 + object. (active voice)**
 
• **object + will/shall + be+ V3 + by + subject. (passive voice)**
 
 
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the **future simple tense**.
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• *Kriya will sew the bag. (active voice)*
 
• *The bag will be sewed by Kriya. (passive voice)**​​*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘A webinar on investment will be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow’ is the correct passive form of the given sentence.

__To keeping__ the photo in front of her, Jia drew the picture.

The correct answer is '**Keeping**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given above sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• In the above-given sentence, '**To keeping**' will be replaced by ‘Keeping’.
 
• As per the general rule, "**keeping**" is used **as a gerund** which makes "**keeping warm**" **a noun phrase**.
 
• "**to keep**" is the **infinitive form**, wherein "**to**" is simply **part of the infinitive**. So, one might say that "**to keep warm**" is a **sentence adverb**.
 
• **both are correct**, but **they differ grammatically**.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• ***Keeping/to keep **her voice conversational, she asked him without looking up. (correct)*
 
• ***To keeping** her voice conversational, she asked him without looking up. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• ​Here in the given above sentence, '**To keeping**' is used**, **which is wrong according to the rule.
 
• According to the explanation and example that are given above, ‘Keeping’ is the most appropriate substitute to the underlined segment.

**Correct sentence:** *Keeping the photo in front of her, Jia drew the picture.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• **"Being kept":** This use of passive voice makes it unclear who is keeping the photo in front of Jia.

 
 
• Is someone else placing it there for her?
 
• Passive voice is not appropriate in this context, because it shifts the focus away from what Jia is doing.
 
• This form would suggest that the photo somehow remained in front of Jia as she drew, but does not indicate that she herself placed or kept it there.
 
 
 
• **"To have kept"**: Using "to have" followed by the past participle of a verb is used to form the perfect infinitive.
 
 
• In this context, it would suggest that the action of Jia keeping the photo in front of her occurred (and finished) before she drew the picture.
 
• It is not the right tense in this context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an example of an **interrogative sentence**. 
 
• The given sentence is in indirect speech. As per the question we have to change it into direct speech. 
 
• Basic rules for changing or converting **indirect speech into direct speech**:​
 
 
• The **commas(,)**, **inverted commas(")**, and the **exclamation mark are added**.
 
• In the first part of the sentence, the verb "**asked**" will be changed to "**said to**" in the direct speech.
 
• Remove the **conjunction "if", **because **'if' conjunction** is not used in the direct speech.
 
• 'could**' will be changed into 'Can' in the direct speech. 
 
• '**he**' will be changed into 'you' in the direct speech.
 
• '**her**' will be changed into 'my' in the direct speech.
 
• A reported question **(?)** is when we tell someone what another person asked.
 
 
 
• This is the direct and indirect speech rule for the interrogative sentence.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• **​***She asked whether we would come for the party. (indirect speech)*
 
• *She said, "Will you come for the party"? (direct speech)**​*
 
 
 
• *​*Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that She said to the drycleaner, “Can you dry clean my coat in a day’s time?” is the correct direct form of the given sentence.
